sources.entry: cookiecutter - A command-line utility that creates projects from cookiecutters (project templates).

summary.one_liner: Cookiecutter is a command-line utility that generates new projects from project templates (cookiecutters) that prompt the user for variable values.
summary.what_it_does: Cookiecutter takes a template directory or a remote template (such as a GitHub repo using the gh: prefix) and prompts the user for values defined in cookiecutter.json, then generates a project from those answers. Templates can be local paths or GitHub-hosted repos. It can also be called from Python via cookiecutter.main. The README says templates can be written for any language or framework, since a template is a directory of variables. Pre-prompt, pre-generate, and post-generate hooks (shell or Python) can run setup steps such as git init or dependency installs. The README lists several special templates, including cookiecutter-pypackage, cookiecutter-django, cookiecutter-pytest-plugin, and cookiecutter-plone-starter.
use_cases: Generate a new Python package project from a template
Scaffold a Django project from a shared template
Create a project skeleton from a local template directory
Build boilerplate for Terraform, Rust, or docs sites from templates
Generate projects programmatically from Python code
Run pre- and post-generation setup hooks for new projects
notable: Works with GitHub-hosted templates via the short gh: prefix
Templates are defined by a cookiecutter.json file that declares prompts and defaults
Supports pre-prompt, pre-generate, and post-generate hooks in shell or Python
Can be used as a CLI tool or imported as a Python library
caveats: README lists Python 3.10 to 3.14 as supported versions
Documentation on the README is sparse for detailed usage; it links to external docs
Community support is through external channels such as Stack Overflow, Discord, and issues; enterprise support is a separate contact
